quotes.text: Terrace, now subdivided into flats. 1824-8, alterations to attic storey mid-late C20. Architects Amon Wilds and C.A.Busby.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1204829, Details, opening sentence

quotes.text: Stucco over brick, roofs of slate.
Plan: terrace of 6 units abutting block of flats to east.

3 storeys over basement plus attic, with additional storey in centre 6 bays, 3:3:6:3:3 bays, mainly sash windows without glazing bars, some French casement windows, full-height bow fronts to penultimate 3 bays east and west, other bays distinguished by use of giant Ionic order, (pilasters frame the outer bays but the centre is all columns), moulded entablature and minimal pediment over central 2 bays, rusticated ground floor except to central 6 bays.
HOVE TQ2904SE BRUNSWICK TERRACE 579-1/23/22 (North side) 24/03/50 Nos.1-6 (Consecutive) and attached railings GV I

note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026. A group record: four Grade I entries cover the terrace and the survey block is the easternmost, Nos 1-6. A CAUTION for anyone extending this record: Historic England also lists a DIFFERENT 'Brunswick Terrace' at 39-63 Kings Road (entry 1319313, Grade II, 'A terrace of 13 houses. Circa 1800, 3 storeys and basements, London stock brick'), which is neither this terrace nor stuccoed nor by Wilds and Busby. It was read here and deliberately not used.
